lots.guide_summary: Two close Gowans SOLD results, $100 (Dec 2025) and $115 (Oct 2025) hammer, all AUD. No unsold or asking evidence. Modern student violins make $40 to $60; labelled or named instruments have made $160 to $340.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD $100 / 1.198 = $83.47, rounded down to $80 hammer ($95.84 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $100 at local auction from the two close SOLD results; less about 15% seller commission and fees ($15) and $0 postage (local pickup resale) = $85; $85 / 2.396 = $35.48, rounded down to $35 hammer. The bridge being off and the worn top argue for staying at or under these figures.
lots.confidence_reason: Clear identification as an old trade violin and 2 close Gowans SOLD results opened with photos viewed, but no label or maker mark readable, and condition (bridge off, possible cracks or loose seams, sound post) cannot be judged from one photo.
lots.condition: Top varnish heavily worn and dirty, scratches and possible small edge wear, bridge not in place and strings slack, fingerboard and tailpiece present, scroll intact. Case scuffed with worn corners but lining intact. Two bows, hair state unknown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Enlarged: no bridge visible, strings loose; no label visible through f-holes at this resolution. Hidersine rosin box and King British steel strings packet suggest UK or Australian use mid 20th century. Two bows in lid, frogs dark, no stamps readable.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there a label inside the f-hole (maker or Stradivarius copy, country)? Is the bridge in the case, is the sound post standing, and are there any cracks in the top or open seams? Are the bows haired and are either stamped?
